title: Cap. 6 Arg. 8: Proper vivifying grace—faith, conversion, regeneration; Augustine's colors
pass_a_gloss: There are also other supernatural gifts which bring to those who have them the state of salvation, such as a good Will, Faith, Conversion, Regeneration; to speak briefly, those things which belong only to human beings inserted into Christ and reconciled to God. And these are the things which Augustine judges ought to be designated properly by the name of the grace of Christ: but those former things, namely the preaching and knowledge of Christian doctrine, he reduces to this grace of Christ properly so called only insofar as they serve to produce and promote the same. In the book On the Grace of Christ he expressly labors to show that under this name there comes not the illumination of the mind or the stirring of the will, but the very gift of faith and of a good will (chapters 10, 47; Epistle 99). He paints this grace of Christ in living colors and calls it the grace by which we are justified from iniquity and by which we are saved from infirmity; a grace which we have least in common with the ungodly, but that by which we are sons of God. Now let us hear the testimonies of the Fathers.
pass_b_english: Other supernatural gifts actually bring the state of salvation: a good will, faith, conversion, regeneration—in short, what belongs only to people grafted into Christ and reconciled to God. Those, Augustine says, deserve the name "grace of Christ" in the proper sense. Preaching and knowledge of Christian doctrine he refers to that proper grace only so far as they help produce and advance it. In On the Grace of Christ he makes the point expressly: the name does not mean mere lighting of the mind or stirring of the will, but the gift of faith itself and of a good will. He paints that grace in bright colors—the grace by which we are justified from iniquity and saved from weakness; a grace we barely share with the ungodly, but the grace by which we are children of God. Now for the Fathers' own words.
source_text: Sunt etiam alia dona supernaturalia quae statum salutis habentibus apportant, qualia sunt bona Voluntas, Fides, Conversio, Regeneratio; ut dicam brevi, ea quae solis hominibus in Christum insertis et Deo reconciliatis conveniunt. Atque haec ea sunt quae Augustinus appellatione gratiae Christi proprie designanda arbitratur: priora autem illa, scilicet praedicationem et cognitionem doctrinae Christianae, ad hanc Christi gratiam proprie dictam eatenus reducit, quatenus inserviunt eidem producendae et promovendae. In libro De gratia Christi id ex professo agit ut ostendat, hoc nomine venire non illuminationem mentis aut excitationem voluntatis, sed ipsam fidem et bonae voluntatis donationem, cap. 10, 47; Epist. 99. Hanc gratiam Christi vivis coloribus depingit atque appellat, gratiam qua justificamur ab iniquitate, et qua salvamur ab infirmitate; gratiam quam cum impiis minime communem habemus, sed eam qua filii Dei sumus. Jam Patrum testimonia audiamus.
